essence: Devotion's excess gives mind: contemplating her, Śiva.
Voidness meditated in all things: even knowing calms.
Neither pure nor impure in Śambhu's view: thought-free happy.
Bhairava everywhere in common things: nondual, no beyond.
Enemy same as friend, honor same as dishonor: happy.
Neither hatred nor passion contemplated: brahman glides middle.
Unknowable, ungraspable, void: as Bhairava — awakening rises.
Wherever mind goes, that instant leaving non-standing: waveless.
Fear resounds all in wholeness: Bhairava's word, Śiva.

rasa.justification: Devotion produces the mind but lands in calm; equalities of enemy/friend and pure/impure flatten all reaction; even fear dissolves into word and waveless — every member ends quieter than it starts.

sections.SUMMARY: The equalizing-block: devotion's excess arising as mind to contemplate her — Śaṅkarī's power — then voidness meditated everywhere calming even knowing; pure/impure both refused in Śambhu-view leaving thought-free happiness; Bhairava in every common thing, nothing beyond, nondual going; enemy and friend, honor and dishonor equal under brahma's fullness; hatred and passion not contemplated so brahman glides in the middle; the fourfold ungraspable contemplated as Bhairava awakening at that end; mind entering the skyless from every sky; mind's going met at each instant by leaving non-standing until waveless; and even fear resounding all-in-wholeness as Bhairava's word making Śiva.
sections.FUNCTION: Equalizes opposites and anxiety itself — the method becomes non-reaction, wavelessness, word.
sections.KEY TERMS: bhakti-udreka (devotion-excess); śāṅkarī (her power); pāpa-kṣaya (sin-wasting as inner sacrifice); tulyatā (enemy/friend equality); bhaya (fear as material, not enemy); śabda (Bhairava-word as agent).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Devotion (v121) introduces bhakti as practice-mode; secrecy verses approach at p16.
sections.BOUNDARY: No ethics-list here; equality is stated as effect of fullness, not moral rule.
sections.EXPLANATION: The block opens the devotional turn: mind born from devotion's excess is itself the power to contemplate — and immediately calms in voidness wherever looked for. Purity-polarities collapse in Śambhu-view, so happiness needs no purification; Bhairava becomes ubiquity (common things, no higher beyond), and equality follows from brahma's fullness rather than effort — enemy, friend, honor, dishonor stand alike. Then the two-way subtraction: neither hatred nor passion contemplated means brahman glides precisely in the middle. The fourfold-ungraspable list is contemplation's object, ending in awakening; every sky-region yields; each mental exit is met by leaving non-standing until waveless; and fear, the last obstacle, becomes the material in which Bhairava's word — and hence Śiva — is heard.
sections.RELATED: Pāpa/homa implicit (inner sacrifice); cf. VBT vv157-159 secrecy — the body of what must not be shown; Hareesh closing-verses analysis.
